name: Osteowell
subtitle: Skeleton, joints, fractures
shortDescription: A real 3D skeleton to rotate, peel apart and quiz yourself on: 198 bones, landmarks, moving joints and fracture patterns. Works offline.
longDescription:
Learn the skeleton the way it really looks. Osteowell puts 198 separately selectable bones in real-time 3D that you can spin, zoom, peel apart and cut open, then tests you until the names stick.

### Explore in 3D
- Rotate and zoom an adult skeleton with realistic bone materials and soft lighting.
- Tap any bone to see its name, type, landmarks and neighbours.
- Explode the skeleton region by region, isolate one bone, or slide a cutting plane through the body to open bones: spongy bone in the ends and vertebrae, the hollow marrow canal in long-bone shafts.
- Show or hide the skull, spine, ribs, arm, forearm and hand, pelvis and thigh, and leg and foot. Show only the left or right side.

### Zoom In
- Zoom from the whole skeleton into a thigh bone cut across the shaft, with a live scale bar, and see the thick ring of compact bone around the marrow canal.

### Landmarks That You Can See
- Pins mark the greater trochanter, the olecranon, the acromion, the mastoid process and many more, placed on the 3D bone itself.
- Every bone has a clear summary, key features, articulations and study notes.

### Joints in Motion
- Move the shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip, knee and ankle with a slider or press Play, and see typical ranges of motion.
- Read how each joint is classified, which movements it allows and what stabilises it.

### Fractures in 3D
- Break a real bone mesh and slide from reduced to displaced. Adjust angulation, twist and shortening to learn the words used to describe a fracture.
- 28 fracture patterns and named fractures: transverse, spiral, comminuted, greenstick, Colles, scaphoid, Jones, Jefferson and more.
- Scrub a healing timeline from haematoma to callus to remodelling.

### Quiz By Region
- Name the highlighted bone, find a bone by tapping it in 3D, name the landmark pin, recognise a fracture pattern or name a joint.
- Spaced repetition brings weak bones back sooner. Daily goal, streak and mastery by region.

### Built for Study
- Works offline, no account needed.
- A- and A+ buttons make text bigger on every reading screen, and the app follows your system text size.
- iPhone and iPad layouts.
- An Accuracy and sources page lists the references and known simplifications, and every screen has a Report an error link.

### Education Only
Osteowell is a study aid. It does not diagnose, treat or give medical advice. Anatomy varies between people.
